content.value_statement: Competitive analysis often becomes scattered across competitor notes, pricing tables, and positioning ideas. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through structured frameworks that turn market evidence into clear strategy.
actual_capabilities: Applies Porter's Five Forces to assess industry pressure and market attractiveness.
Builds positioning maps using dimensions such as price, complexity, segment, and service model.
Creates competitor profiles covering product, pricing, go-to-market, strengths, weaknesses, and likely moves.
Compares pricing tiers and packaging to identify gaps and signals.
Guides differentiation, beachhead selection, and sustainable advantage testing.
limitations: Does not fetch live competitor data or verify current pricing without user-provided sources.
Depends on accurate inputs about products, customers, and competitors.
Provides strategic analysis, not legal, financial, or investment advice.
Framework outputs need validation with customer interviews and market data.

use_cases.title: Map a Startup Market
use_cases.description: Identify direct competitors, substitutes, and viable beachhead segments before launch.

use_cases.title: Sharpen Product Positioning
use_cases.description: Compare offers, pricing, and messaging to define stronger differentiation.

use_cases.title: Prepare Strategy Reviews
use_cases.description: Create structured competitor profiles and advantage tests for leadership planning.

prompt_templates.title: Identify Competitors
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me identify direct competitors, indirect competitors, and substitutes for [product]. Ask for any missing context first.

prompt_templates.title: Apply Five Forces
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Porter's Five Forces to analyze [market]. Rate each force, explain the evidence needed, and list the main strategic risks.

prompt_templates.title: Build Positioning Map
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a positioning map for [company] against [competitors]. Recommend two axes, explain the white space, and test whether it matters to buyers.

prompt_templates.title: Create Competitive Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Conduct a full competitive landscape analysis for [company]. Include competitor profiles, pricing comparison, differentiation options, beachhead market, and monitoring cadence.

output_examples.input: Analyze the market for a new AI email marketing platform.
output: Direct rivals include established email platforms with automation and analytics.
Substitutes include CRM workflows, manual campaigns, and ecommerce platform tools.
A likely white space is AI-assisted personalization for small teams with limited marketing staff.

output_examples.input: Compare our pricing against two SaaS competitors.
output: Your entry tier sits between the two alternatives, which signals mid-market value.
The enterprise tier lacks clear packaging, so buyers may compare it only on price.
A stronger recommendation is to tie packaging to onboarding, support, and usage limits.

output_examples.input: Find a defensible advantage for a workflow automation product.
output: Network effects are weak unless templates or integrations improve with adoption.
Switching costs may be defensible if customers depend on historical workflow data.
The strongest test is whether the advantage matters to buyers and is hard to copy within two years.

best_practices: Bring current competitor data, source links, and customer evidence before asking for recommendations.
Separate direct competitors, substitutes, and future entrants before ranking threats.
Validate positioning claims with buyer interviews, win/loss notes, and pricing evidence.
anti_patterns: Using the framework to invent market facts without evidence.
Comparing feature lists without linking them to customer needs or willingness to pay.
Treating a one-time analysis as a substitute for ongoing competitive monitoring.

faq.question: What inputs should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide your product, target customer, competitors, pricing, known customer pains, and any source links you trust.

faq.question: Can it research live competitor websites?
faq.answer: The skill provides frameworks and analysis prompts. Live research depends on the tool environment and user-provided sources.

faq.question: Which strategy frameworks does it use?
faq.answer: It uses Porter's Five Forces, Blue Ocean Strategy, positioning maps, competitor profiles, pricing analysis, and advantage testing.

faq.question: Is it only for SaaS companies?
faq.answer: No. The examples include SaaS, but the frameworks can support many product, service, and market categories.

faq.question: Can it create a final strategy recommendation?
faq.answer: Yes. It can synthesize evidence into positioning, differentiation, beachhead, pricing, and monitoring recommendations.

faq.question: How should I use the results?
faq.answer: Treat outputs as structured analysis. Validate them with current market data, customer interviews, and internal business constraints.
